newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian, 2 unions say chance of deal today.
newsitem.headline: Canadian, 2 unions say chance of deal today.

text.p: Officials from Canadian Airlines Corp and unions representing its pilots and machinists said on Monday that there was a chance of a deal today to save the carrier.

They made the comments after meeting Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson. But they added that the participation of the Canadian Auto Workers union and the Canadian Union of Public Employees needed to be secured for the plan to advance.

The unions and Canadian president Kevin Benson presented a plan to Anderson but would not detail its contents. The unions in the past had urged the federal government to consider easing fuel taxes and other measures to help the airline.

Anderson said after the meeting that the rescue plan had the support of four out of Canadian's six unions and he repeated that the backing of the CAW and CUPE was vital. He aimed to meet with officials of those two unions later.
"There seems to be a willingness (for the government to help) there," said Dave Ritchie of the International Association of Machinists after meeting Anderson.

"We figure this is going to be an ongoing process for the next couple of hours anyway or maybe this whole day. But we're upbeat that we can come to a deal. And we believe that the airline will fly for a long time coming," Ritchie said.
"...The government has to come to the table," he said. "One of our requests is that the governments are going to be prepared to share some pain as well."
The machinists and pilots unions had voiced support for a restructuring plan proposed by the airline that called for wage cuts. CUPE and CAW oppose the wage reduction.
"I believe we are going to be able to come to a consensus here and come to a deal," Ritchie said.
Mike Lynch of the Canadian Air Line Pilots Association said he expected to have further talks with Anderson later in the day. He said the government gave the proposal a "sympathetic ear."

Benson said he hoped for a deal on Monday but that the lack of support from the two key unions was a "problem." "Time is running out fast," he said. Without an agreement by Wednesday, "I think the whole plan starts to unravel."

He said he hoped that CUPE and CAW would understand that the proposed plan was as complex and comprehensive as the government would support. Asked if he was confident a deal could be reached on Monday, Benson said, "I am not confident. I am hopeful. I've been hopeful for quite a while."
Benson said there would also be meetings with Alberta and British Columbia government officials.

Anderson described the meeting as "positive." But he said the government could not act until a restructuring plan won support from all six unions and the company. He said the government would have to review the proposals.
Anderson seemed to downplay hopes of a deal on Monday, saying that a range of participants including Canadian's minority owner AMR Corp and other creditors would also have to be involved.

But from government's point of view, "everything is on the table in the sense we've only excluded reregulation," he said. He also repeated reservations about the possibility of AMR raising its stake. Anderson said a full deal was possible by Wednesday. "I am hopeful...we will have quick movement today and tomorrow," he said. "I'd be delighted to have an agreement today...but we're not at that point yet."
